title: What Does the Bible Say About Cussing and Swearing? 26 Verses
description: Is cussing a sin? What the Bible says about foul language, cursing, taking God's name in vain and oaths, with 26 verses.
keywords: what does the bible say about cussing
bible verses about watching your words
summary: The Bible never uses the word cuss, but it speaks plainly about the language that word describes. Paul tells believers to let no corrupt speech come out of their mouths, only what builds others up (Ephesians 4:29), and to put away anger, wrath, slander and shameful talk (Colossians 3:8). Forms of swear appear 71 times in 61 verses of the World English Bible, and most are about oaths and taking God's name lightly: Exodus 20:7 forbids misusing the name of Yahweh, and Jesus told his hearers to let their yes be yes and their no be no (Matthew 5:37). The Bible gives no list of banned words. It asks about what the words do, to God and to the people who hear them.

faqs.a: The Bible does not list particular words, but it condemns corrupt, filthy and abusive speech (Ephesians 4:29, 5:4, Colossians 3:8) and warns that people will give account for every careless word (Matthew 12:36). Many Christians treat profanity as falling under those verses, particularly when it is aimed at people or uses God's name lightly. Others separate rude words from the sins the verses name. The test the verses give is whether the words build up or tear down.

faqs.q: What does taking the Lord's name in vain mean?
faqs.a: The third commandment says not to take the name of Yahweh your God in vain (Exodus 20:7). The Hebrew points to using his name for empty or false purposes: swearing false oaths, using his name as a curse or a casual exclamation, or speaking it without meaning. Jesus extended the concern to oaths in general (Matthew 5:33-37).

faqs.q: Does the Bible say not to swear at all?
faqs.a: Jesus said not to swear at all, neither by heaven nor by earth, and to let your word be yes or no (Matthew 5:34-37), and James repeats it (James 5:12). The context is oath-taking: making a promise sound more binding by invoking something sacred. The same Bible records God himself swearing, and Paul calling God to witness, so Christians read the teaching as a call to be a person whose plain word is enough.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about the power of words?
faqs.a: Proverbs 18:21 says death and life are in the power of the tongue, and James 3:9-10 asks how blessing and cursing can come from the same mouth. Proverbs 15:1 says a gentle answer turns away wrath. The consistent teaching is that speech has weight, and that believers are to use it to bless.
